package_info.why_malicious: A critical bug in npm v5.7.0 causes the package manager to recursively change ownership of crucial system directories (such as /etc, /usr, /boot) to the invoking user when run with sudo, leading to system instability, application failures, and unbootable systems. This behavior is highly destructive and unexpected for a package manager.

execution_context.trigger: postinstall/command-line (when running any npm command with sudo as a non-root user)
execution_context.file_location: npm CLI core logic (exact file not specified, but within npm v5.7.0 source code)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Recursively chown (change ownership) of / and critical system directories to the invoking user when running 'sudo npm' commands.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: The code erroneously changes the ownership of system directories (such as /etc, /usr, /boot) to the non-root user running npm with sudo, recursively affecting the entire filesystem.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Package managers should never alter ownership of system directories outside their own install scope. Recursively changing ownership of / or critical directories is highly destructive and not a legitimate operation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm behavior is to install or update JavaScript packages, not to modify system-level directory ownership. This action breaks the principle of least privilege and system integrity.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: A legitimate use might be a system administration tool designed to fix permissions, but never as part of a package manager's normal operation.
key_indicators: Triggered by running 'sudo npm' as a non-root user

attack_chain.action: User runs any npm command with sudo (e.g., 'sudo npm --help' or 'sudo npm update -g') as a non-root user.
attack_chain.leads_to: npm recursively changes ownership of critical system directories to the invoking user.

attack_chain.action: System directories (/etc, /usr, /boot, etc.) have their ownership changed, breaking system functionality.
attack_chain.leads_to: System instability, application failures, or unbootable system.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected recursive chown operations on /, /etc, /usr, /boot triggered by npm commands
npm process running with sudo and performing filesystem ownership changes outside its install directory
file_indicators: Ownership of /etc, /usr, /boot, or other system directories changed to a non-root user
Audit logs showing chown operations initiated by npm processes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm processes running with sudo that initiate recursive chown operations on system directories. Use auditd or similar tools to detect and alert on ownership changes to critical directories, especially when the owner is set to a non-root user. Check for recent changes in directory ownership after npm upgrades or installations.
